title: Exclude a literal P104 e=1 frame lift by the signed-idle kernel
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

For the exact e=1, three-host signed frame from #7861, the specified reflection has nonzero contact products at every candidate host stage. It cannot be one of the retained signed caller's IDLE_ODD events, which require a nonempty stage set. The obstruction permits enlarged masks and intervening LAMBDA normalizers. The wider abstract #7852 datatype admits an empty idle set, and a different thin factorization remains open.

## Task and overlap

Uses #7861 at 5cbe00f354aae5923205ec68370ddaa5296c2ea7, #7852 at 41beda1d6435760dc99e38bd7e65f36798aad212 and the signed checker in #7113 at 07a76c5e2738882c0cb322278e56f6cae3c9885d. #7869 gives separate excess-thin type and decomposition examples. This isolates one concrete frame and its prescribed transfers.

## Validation and credit

The standalone python3 -B check.py with SymPy authenticates source data and recomputes the fixed-gauge contact products and host prefixes. A relocated copy matched and rejected a corrupted source. The proof is a paper application of the published kernel condition. Research and tests were AI-assisted with Codex. Thanks to DreamingOfClouds and the #7113 caller contributors.

## Open next questions

A broader legal-word restriction or a constructive replacement factorization remains open.
